analysis.title: Calling It (Again): AI CDS Trading Explodes As FT Notices The Hottest Job On Wall Street
key_insights: Morgan Stanley data cited by the FT shows more than $9B a week of CDS on Oracle, SpaceX, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Broadcom and Nvidia traded in September, up from under $2B in July. That is about 4.5x in two months.
AI-linked companies have raised an estimated $466B of debt in 2026 versus $101B in the same period of 2025 (Morgan Stanley). Issuance has slowed from June's peak but protection buying has continued.

Single-name AI CDS spreads are at or near records: Meta 108bp, Nvidia 101bp, SpaceX 226bp (110bp at the late-June open), Oracle 322bp (144bp at the start of the year). Alphabet and Amazon protection is also at all-time highs.
Buyers fall into two groups per Morgan Stanley's Jim Caron: real-money bond investors hedging books, and multi-asset and equity speculators seeking a cheap hedge on technology exposure.

Goldman's IG desk reported AI-related USD IG spreads 25bp wider than non-AI peers versus 6bp historically, with synthetic CDS volume at 20x reference obligations. That points to hedging by accounts that do not own the bonds.

Goldman FICC says AI single-name CDS volume is up 400% y/y, the liquid universe has grown from 4 to 10-12 names, and notional per name has gone from $50-100mm a week to hundreds of millions a day. Monthly AI CDS volume topped $10B in September, about 8x a year earlier.

Goldman's Alisha Pasi reported a record level of nontraditional-account inquiry on CRWV debt and ORCL CDS, and Goldman set up a dedicated AI cross-cap-structure investor call. Oracle bonds and CDS moved 30-45bp wider last week while IG cash widened about 3bp.
Hedging has started to spread to holders of AI paper. Financials and insurance CDS was bid last week on concerns about investment concentration in those entities as the AI trade sold off.
Index hedges are losing precision. CDX IG widened only 4.4bp to 62.5bp last week while key single names moved about 30bp a day, so investors are shifting to single-name CDS.

CDS is replacing equity puts as the hedge of choice. SocGen's Manish Kabra says equity puts on such a volatile sector are extremely expensive, and SocGen's 4Q26 outlook lists Long US Hyperscalers CDS as a key trade under the heading watch CDS not EPS.

Morgan Stanley (Oct 1) has its AI CDS basket about 45bp wide of CDX IG and calls buying protection its preferred way to play AI in credit derivatives. It expects continued non-economic hedging demand from banks managing counterparty exposure.

CoreWeave 5Y CDS is around 1,090bp, costing $1.82M upfront plus $125,000 a quarter per $10M of protection. It closed at a record 1,117bp on Oct 14, which the author says implies about 63% odds of default within five years. HSBC set a $39 target on the stock.

Chip makers offering seller financing and guarantees to buyers have drawn CDS volume. Rolling one-month volumes in Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom CDS were up 10x, and Broadcom CDS hit a record 122 after reports it sought up to $100B in an off-balance-sheet SPV.

The author argues demand is structural because every new bond, SPV, lease guarantee and vendor-financing deal creates a holder or counterparty needing a hedge. The author expects the next leg of any AI unwind to show up in CDS first.

market_movers.rationale: HSBC set a $39 target on CoreWeave, warning that the more it invests, the more the value destruction. The note is cited as contradicting Goldman's upgrade of the stock.

trade_ideas.rationale: SocGen says to watch CDS not EPS, as hyperscaler CDS has more than tripled since early 2025 and multiples have compressed with it.

trade_ideas.description: Buy protection on the AI CDS basket versus CDX IG
trade_ideas.rationale: Morgan Stanley calls buying protection its preferred way to play AI in credit derivatives, citing increasing needs for non-economic hedging to manage counterparty exposure.

risk_factors: Circular financing in AI, where the weakest link could deteriorate the system (Polus Capital's Robert Dafforn).
Off-balance-sheet SPVs, lease guarantees and vendor financing create new counterparties that need hedges.
Contagion to financials and insurers that hold AI paper, with CDS on those names already bid.
CoreWeave distress, with CDS above 1,000bp where expected recovery pricing takes over and capital markets access reported frozen.
Weak AI-related listings, such as Elice's 32% drop on its Korean IPO debut.
Continued heavy AI debt issuance, with Goldman forecasting more hyperscaler and project-finance supply in 2027.
charts_described: SocGen chart shows hyperscaler 5Y CDS has more than tripled since early 2025 while forward multiples have compressed.
Goldman FICC chart of monthly AI CDS volume topping $10 billion in September, roughly 8x a year earlier.
vol_and_positioning: Single-name AI CDS protection demand is heavy. Goldman reports synthetic CDS volume at 20x reference obligations and a record level of nontraditional-account inquiry on ORCL CDS and CRWV debt.

Flows in the index were primarily macro accounts adding hedges and real-money investors staying defensive, versus hedge-fund short covering. With dispersion rising, the index is a less precise expression of the risk investors own.
CDX IG widened 4.4bp to 62.5bp last week while Oracle bonds and CDS moved 30-45bp wider and the 30Y hyperscaler basket is at its year-to-date wides.
Hyperscaler 5Y CDS has more than tripled since early 2025 and forward multiples have compressed alongside it (SocGen).
Equity puts on AI names are described as extremely expensive, which is pushing equity-focused accounts to hedge with CDS.
cross_bank_references: Morgan Stanley, whose data anchors the FT piece, has been on the same page.
Which, again, is precisely what Goldman told clients back in August.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman upgraded CoreWeave, and the stock can be bought on dips.
tension_points.bear_case: HSBC sets a $39 target, saying the more it invests the more the value destruction. CDS at about 1,090bp implies heavy default pricing.

tension_points.bull_case: Optimists say record CDS volumes just reflect a deeper, healthier hedging market.
tension_points.bear_case: The author compares real money returning to single-name CDS after 15 years to 2007, and expects the bond market to lead the stock market lower.

theme_stances.key_argument: The bond market is ahead of the stock market, and the next leg of the AI unwind shows up in CDS first.
CoreWeave is the weakest link for now, and its CDS pricing has moved to expected recovery.
theme_stances.evidence: whatever the weakest link is will actually start to deteriorate the system
